newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First rules out foreign control of media.
newsitem.headline: NZ First rules out foreign control of media.

text.p: Opposition New Zealand First would not allow "overseas control" of the media, a spokesperson for the party said on Tuesday in the wake of the full bid for Wilson and Horton by Independent Newspapers Plc of Ireland.
He said it would be up to the Overseas Investment Commission (OIC) and the anti-monopolies Commerce Commission to prevent foreign control, but the concern was more for competition.
"There is a view that the current legislation would prevent (control) through normal competition laws," the spokesman said.
"If not, the Commerce Act would be strengthened to achieve that."

New Zealand First plans to create a new organisation, the International Investment Commission, to take over the role and responsibilities of the OIC and some of the current Commerce Commission functions.
It also plans to restrict foreign interests in "strategic" assets to 25 percent and require holdings above that level to be sold only to New Zealanders, although there would be no forced sales.
The spokesman said the media was not one of the strategic assets covered by New Zealand First's policy.
He said some purchases by foreign interests did not affect competition. "Aggregation of ownership is the major concern."

The left-wing Alliance earlier condemned the Independent bid as a form of cultural imperialism. The main opposition Labour Party said the bid should not be affected by its own policy to examine foreign and cross-media ownership.
